section-navy6.eyebrow: WHEN VENEERS ARE THE WRONG CHOICE
section-navy6.h2: Not all veneers are the same thing.
section-navy6.text: "Veneer" covers two quite different treatments, and the difference shows up years later. Composite bonding is resin shaped onto the tooth in the chair: quicker and cheaper, but more opaque, more prone to staining, and typically lasting around four to eight years. Porcelain is made to fit you, holds its colour, and lasts ten to twenty years or more with proper care.
section-navy6.text-link2: Find out which suits your case
section7.benefit-text: Veneers sit at the gum line, so the gums have to be healthy before anything is designed or prepared.
section7.benefit-text2: A veneer covers a tooth; it does not repair one. Anything structural is treated first.
section7.benefit-text3: Grinding and clenching shorten the life of any restoration, so how you use your teeth is part of the assessment.
section7.benefit-text4: If the goal is straighter teeth rather than covered ones, Invisalign® or Six Month Smiles is usually the better answer.
section-sand8.h2: What a designed smile can look like.

section9.h2: How a veneer case actually runs.
section9.journey-text: Gums, decay and bite are checked, and Dr. Bennett says whether veneers are the right route for what you want to change.
section9.journey-text2: A small portion of enamel is removed from the front of each treated tooth so the veneer sits flush, and the design is settled with you.
section9.journey-text3: The veneers are made to your agreed shade, shape and proportion and finished in the practice's own lab.
section9.journey-text4: The finished veneers are fitted and bonded at the second visit, and the bite is checked before you leave.

faq.q: How much do veneers cost in Arvada, Colorado?
faq.a: Porcelain veneers typically cost $1,200-$2,500 per tooth, depending on the complexity of your case and number of veneers needed. We offer flexible financing options and accept most dental insurance. Our membership club provides additional savings for uninsured patients.‍

faq.q: How long do porcelain veneers last?
faq.a: With proper care, porcelain veneers can last 10-15 years or longer. Maintain them with regular brushing, flossing, and dental checkups. Avoid biting hard objects and consider a nightguard if you grind your teeth.

Yes! Modern porcelain veneers are custom-designed to match your facial features, skin tone, and natural tooth color. We use digital smile design to preview your results and ensure you love your new look before treatment begins.

No. We use local anesthesia during tooth preparation to ensure your comfort. Most patients experience only minor sensitivity after the procedure, which resolves within a few days. Over-the-counter pain relievers manage any discomfort.‍

faq.q: How are veneers different from crowns?
faq.a: Veneers cover only the front surface of teeth and require minimal tooth preparation. Crowns cover the entire tooth and require more extensive reduction. Veneers are ideal for cosmetic improvements, while crowns are better for teeth with significant structural damage.‍

Veneers can correct minor misalignment and create the appearance of straighter teeth. However, they're not a substitute for orthodontic treatment if you have significant bite issues or severe crowding. We'll assess your situation during consultation.‍

faq.q: Do I need veneers on all my teeth?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Many patients get 6-8 veneers on their upper front teeth (the "smile zone") for dramatic results. We'll recommend the number of veneers needed to achieve your desired outcome based on your goals and budget.

faq.q: What happens if a veneer chips or breaks?
faq.a: While porcelain veneers are durable, they can chip or crack if subjected to excessive force. If this happens, contact us immediately. Depending on the damage, we may be able to repair or will need to replace the veneer.

faq.q: Can I get veneers if I have gum disease?
faq.a: You must have healthy gums before getting veneers. We'll treat any gum disease first, then proceed with veneers once your oral health is optimal. This ensures the best long-term results.
